title: Exasol Nano (Linux / WSL / Windows runtime)
tagline: The local Exasol database, running as a container.
role: On Linux, WSL and Windows the kit runs Exasol Nano in Docker or Podman. macOS uses Exasol Personal natively instead. Everything above the runtime - exapump, MCP, pyexasol - is identical.

commands.summary: Start the container (creating it if needed).
Stop it. The data volume is kept.

environment: EXAKIT_AUTOSTART_CHANGE=1|0 pre-answers the question for scripts

environment.name: EXAKIT_DB_PORT
environment.effect: Use an alternate host port, e.g. 8564, when 8563 is taken.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NANO_CONTAINER
environment.effect: Name of the container (default exasol-nano). Set it before installing to keep a Windows and a WSL install apart: Docker Desktop with WSL integration is one engine, so both otherwise share this container.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NANO_VOLUME
environment.effect: Name of the data volume (default exasol-nano-data). That volume is the database; set it alongside EXAKIT_NANO_CONTAINER.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NANO_READY_TIMEOUT
environment.effect: Seconds to wait for the database to report ready (default 600). Raise it on a slow machine.

troubleshooting.symptom: Docker is installed but not running
troubleshooting.remedy: macOS/Windows: start Docker Desktop, or run: podman machine start. Linux: sudo systemctl start docker - there is no Podman machine on Linux, so for Podman check the user-namespace ranges instead: grep $(id -un) /etc/subuid /etc/subgid.

troubleshooting.symptom: A WSL install and a Windows install are fighting over one database
troubleshooting.remedy: Docker Desktop with WSL integration is one engine and both default to the container exasol-nano, so the second install takes over the first one's container and either uninstall removes it. Pick one path per machine, or set EXAKIT_NANO_CONTAINER and EXAKIT_NANO_VOLUME on one of them before installing.
